title: Frustration of contractual purpose
summary: Frustration concerns an event that destroys the principal purpose of the exchange for a party even though the promised performance may remain physically possible.
notes:
In Krell, rooms could still be supplied, but cancellation of the coronation procession defeated the shared purpose for which the particular daytime use had been arranged. The court considered the transaction’s setting and the parties’ understanding rather than requiring an express sentence naming that purpose.

A party’s private hope or ordinary loss of profit does not necessarily define the bargain’s principal purpose. Determine whether the purpose was sufficiently shared or known, whether the disruption was fundamental, and whether the party claiming excuse bore the risk. Distinguish frustration from impossibility: the former asks what performance would now achieve, while the latter asks whether the undertaking can be performed.

topics.frustration: An event may defeat the agreed purpose without making delivery impossible.
